Image 3 is a three-view sheet; the user explicitly APPROVES the SHOULDER SHAPE in its MIDDLE SIDE FIGURE ONLY, and explicitly REJECTS that figure's outward-facing engine. Image 4's green rectangles point to calf FRONT/REAR tread runs. Image 5's green rectangles select rear backpack/fins and rear calf armor. No green boxes, screenshot borders or labels in output. Replace Image 1's extremely thin flat wing strip above the engine with the substantial SWEPT TRIANGULAR SHOULDER/WING HOUSING of the MIDDLE figure in Image 3: a layered graphite triangular wedge with ivory beveled leading-edge frame, orange accent and visible wing-root shoulder armor. This shoulder housing belongs to the bomber upper frame, separated from the core shoulder joint so the arm can move. Preserve the ENGINE DIRECTION already correct in Image 1: cylindrical engine lies fore-aft, intake points LEFT, exhaust points RIGHT. Show the cylindrical side wall under the selected shoulder wedge, with a narrow intake rim toward the front; DO NOT copy the big round fan facing the viewer from Image 3. Shoulder silhouette from Image 3, engine orientation from Image 1. 2. Restore the missing FRONT TREAD RUN on the lower leg. Image 4 left green rectangle is the missing part: a robust BLACK ARTICULATED PADDED CRAWLER BAND must visibly run along the FRONT/leading edge of the calf from just below/behind the knee drill mounting down toward the ankle/top of boot, corresponding to the black front tread visible in the full front master Image 2. Keep the existing correct BACK tread run and rear wheels in Image 1/Image 4 right green rectangle. Preserve the steel knee drill facing LEFT, normal knee joint, black ankle articulation and chunky separate boot/heel structure. Keep the existing correct rear foot/heel tread construction. 3. Make the FRONT and OUTER SIDE leg design more articulated and specific: replace the two huge blank ivory calf slabs with overlapping beveled armor segments, substantial orange load-bearing brackets, recessed charcoal mechanisms, varied-size drive wheels, one or two readable dark vent inserts and a short exposed metallic actuator where it plausibly joins the housing. Organize these as a coherent drill-vehicle module between front/rear tread bands. Keep some calm ivory paint; do NOT add random greeble noise, extra guns, spikes or glowing decorations. Preserve the master front view's panel/color hierarchy and strong long-leg proportions. 4. Integrate only the SIDE-appropriate silhouette of Image 5's approved REAR features: central orange/graphite backpack behind the torso, and the near orange-edged dark vertical tail fin at the back of the shoulder, largely behind the mane. Do not obscure the head, turn it into a new aircraft or add a third side engine. The main wide bomber wings/shoulder system, train-cab forearm shells with nose facing BACK toward elbow, and truly massive steel fists all remain. Do NOT adopt the small fists, slimmer arms or short body of Image 3 or 5. Preserve all unmentioned details of Image 1, especially face, hair, chest/cockpit and arm posing. Crisp clean KINETIC_CEL animation rendering with controlled pressure ink, two-level shadows and block materials, matching the front master. Full crown, mane, shoulder, drill and feet inside the image. No writing, no arrows, no green annotation, no poster effects.
